title: 1987 AHSME Problem 13
statement: A long piece of paper \(5\) cm wide is made into a roll for cash registers by wrapping it \(600\) times around a cardboard tube of diameter \(2\) cm, forming a roll \(10\) cm in diameter. Approximate the length of the paper in meters. (Pretend the paper forms \(600\) concentric circles with diameters evenly spaced from \(2\) cm to \(10\) cm.)

solutions.text:
The average of the first and last diameters is \[ \frac{2+10}{2}=6\text{ cm}. \] Hence the total length is approximately \(600(6\pi)=3600\pi\) cm, or \(36\pi\) meters.

Thus the correct answer is A.
hints: The \(600\) diameters form an arithmetic sequence
Use the average diameter to find the sum of all \(600\) circumferences
